🦉 RAG Tutor — Notebook 1: The Basic Hows & Whys

Building & Visualizing a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System from Scratch

Welcome to Notebook 1 of the interactive RAG curriculum! Inspired by Xuan-Son Nguyen's Code a simple RAG from scratch and interactive explorers from the Marimo Gallery, this notebook demystifies how RAG works using pure Python and an Electric Vehicle knowledge base (data/ev-facts.txt)—before we touch any external vector databases or advanced production pipelines.
Local LLM Backend (http://localhost:9931/v1): 🟢 Llama.app Connected — Connected to Llama.app at http://localhost:9931 (1 model(s) found)

1. Why Do We Need RAG? (The Hallucination & Cutoff Problem)

Large Language Models (LLMs) store general world knowledge inside their weights (parametric memory), but they have three fundamental blind spots:
  1. Private / Internal Data: They have never seen your team's private documents or custom error codes.
  2. Knowledge Cutoffs: They do not know facts created after their training finished.
  3. Confident Hallucinations: Without grounded context, an LLM will often guess or fabricate details.

2. How Retrieval Works: Interactive 2D Vector Compass & Metric Gauges

To find which facts in our knowledge base match a user's question, we convert text into Embedding Vectors (lists of floating-point numbers representing meaning) and measure the angle between them using Cosine Similarity: ||[\text{cosine\_similarity}(A, B) = \frac{A \cdot B}{\|A\| \cdot \|B\|} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i B_i}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i^2} \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n} B_i^2}}||]Drag the sliders below to move 2D vectors A (teal) and B (amber), inspect the orthogonal projection and angle arc ||(\theta||), and compare Cosine Similarity against Dot Product and Euclidean Distance:
🟢 High Semantic Alignment (Same Direction)
Cosine Similarity (Angle-only, scale-invariant) +0.9834 (θ = 10.4°)
Raw Dot Product (A · B) (Sensitive to vector length) +0.9625
Euclidean Distance ‖A − B‖ (Tip-to-tip distance) dist = 0.180 (sim = 0.847)
💡 Visual Intuition: The dashed gray line shows the orthogonal projection of B onto A. Try scaling A from (0.9, 0.0) down to (0.2, 0.0): Dot Product and Euclidean Distance change, but Cosine Similarity stays constant!
